captain-of-industry game sourced

Captain of Industry

An industrial colony builder in which the player reshapes island terrain with excavators and trucks, runs production chains to feed, house, and power a settlement, and spends the Unity its satisfied population generates on edicts, quick builds, and world-map expansion.

2022MaFi GamesFactory / automationcluster c0222 mechanics
this record asyaml sourcemarkdownjson

core loop

designate mining and dumping areas -> trucks haul ore and rock -> smelt and refine into goods -> feed, power, and house the population -> satisfied needs generate Unity -> spend Unity and products on research, edicts, and ship expeditions -> expand and terraform

design notes

Captain of Industry joins a factory game to a settlement whose population is both labor and a consumer: residents need housing, food, water, electricity, healthcare, and household goods, each fully satisfied need yields about one to two Unity per month, and Unity buys edicts, outposts, quick trades, instant construction, and emergency repairs. Every working vehicle and many buildings consume crafted Maintenance I, II, or III; below 75% a monthly breakdown roll begins, reaching 50% at zero, so maintenance is itself a production chain whose failure cascades through the economy. Terrain is a stock of materials: excavators dig inside a Mine Control Tower's area, trucks dump rock and dirt that settle at per-material angles of repose (about 42 degrees for loose dirt to 78 for hardened rock), and dumping reclaims ocean for ports. A ship explores a world map for islands, refugees, and trade partners. Unity works like a political-capital currency earned from welfare, which the taxonomy lacks; this run proposed one.

uses

Goods consumption

Residents consume food, water, electricity, healthcare, and household goods; each fully satisfied need yields Unity, and unmet food or health shrinks the population.

core
uses

Hauling jobs

Trucks are assigned to mines, storages, and buildings and automatically deliver products where they are needed, so fleet size and road layout cap throughput before belts and trains replace them.

core
uses

Production chains

Smelters, refineries, chemical plants, food processors, and assembly lines run recipe chains from iron and copper ore to electronics, fuel, consumer goods, and nuclear fuel across 100+ technologies.

core
uses

Resource extraction

Excavators dig ore, coal, limestone, and rock from designated terrain, while oil rigs, quartz and uranium mines, and water pumps work fixed deposits and outposts.

core
uses

Terraforming

Mining designations inside a Mine Control Tower area lower terrain and dumping designations raise it; loose material settles at per-material angles of repose, retaining walls stabilize slopes, and dumping can reclaim ocean.

core
uses

Wear and breakdown

Working vehicles and buildings consume Maintenance I to III crafted at depots (idle at about a third); below 75% maintenance a breakdown is rolled monthly with chance rising to 50% at zero.

core
uses

Byproducts and waste

Production emits slag, waste, carbon dioxide, wastewater, and spent nuclear fuel that must be dumped, treated, recycled, or stored.

supporting
uses

Conveyor transport

Belts and pipes give high-throughput direct links between machines once truck logistics become a bottleneck.

supporting
uses

Crop cultivation

Farms grow crops for food and industrial inputs, fertilizer boosts yields, and greenhouses grow advanced crops.

supporting
uses

Designation orders

The player paints mining and dumping designations, and excavators and trucks assigned to a Mine Control Tower carry out the work inside its area.

supporting
uses

Building placement

supporting
uses

Machine boosting

Unity is spent on building boosts (0.25 Unity each) that speed up individual buildings.

supporting
uses

Periodic ticks

Unity income, population change, edict costs, and maintenance breakdown rolls resolve monthly.

supporting
uses

Policy toggles

Captain's Office edicts change settlement rules, such as raising population growth by tier, for a monthly Unity cost.

supporting
uses

Political capital

Each fully satisfied settlement need yields about 1 to 2 Unity per month, spent on edicts, outposts, quick trades, instant construction, and emergency repairs.

supporting
uses

Pollution spread

Air and water pollution and unmanaged waste spread disease among the population.

supporting
uses

Power grid

Generators up to nuclear reactors feed the settlement and factories, and residents require electricity as one of their needs.

supporting
uses

Storage and buffers

Storages and loose storage piles buffer materials, and full outputs stall production upstream.

supporting
uses

Tech tree

Research labs consume products and Unity to unlock over 100 technologies from basic smelting to space flight.

uses

Trade routes

Ships explore a world map to discover islands and trading partners; quick trades and recurring contracts exchange goods.
